CHIEF COMPLAINT
Left ankle pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a male presenting with left ankle injury sustained yesterday while taking a walk with his wife. Patient stepped off a curb and landed on the ankle incorrectly. Denies hearing or feeling a pop; describes sensation of ankle feeling stretched and extended. Pain is localized to the lateral (outside) aspect of the ankle and has been present since injury. Patient rated pain as 8/10 without medication and 7/10 with ibuprofen. Initially able to ambulate back to house though with significant pain. Denies substantial prior ankle injuries. Since injury, patient has been managing symptoms with ibuprofen, elevation, ice, and weight-bearing avoidance.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Ankle pain is primary complaint. No other systems reviewed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No substantial prior ankle injuries

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen (over-the-counter, patient-initiated)

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient walks regularly with wife. Works from home.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Stable, slightly elevated (attributed to pain)
Focused examination of left ankle: Ecchymosis and bruising over lateral malleolus, swelling and edema present, tenderness to palpation on lateral side, soft tissue swelling. No laxity appreciated in joint. No bony tenderness on palpation of foot.
Neurovascular examination of left foot: Capillary refill brisk (less than 3 seconds), strong dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally, motor and sensation intact and equal bilaterally.

RESULTS
X-ray of left ankle: No fracture or bony abnormalities

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Left ankle sprain of lateral ligament complex. Continue RICE protocol (rest, ice, elevation, compression). Air cast provided for ankle stabilization. Crutches prescribed; patient to stay off leg but begin walking as tolerated when able. Continue NSAIDs for pain and swelling management. Significant improvement expected over first 4-7 days. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks. Patient instructed to return if experiencing severe pain or other concerns.
